name.text: Finding the mistake in a square count

questiontext.text:
Kendi estimated the area of a fish pond on a farm in Kirinyaga from a plan drawn on squares. Each square stands for \({@s@}\,\text{m}\) by \({@s@}\,\text{m}\). She counted \({@F@}\) full squares and \({@P@}\) part squares. Her working:

Step 1: number of squares \(\approx {@sh1@}\).
Step 2: area of one square \(= {@sh2@}\,\text{m}^2\).
Step 3: area \(\approx {@sh1@} \times {@sh2@} = {@sh3@}\,\text{m}^2\).

Her working has one mistake.

(a) Which statement describes her mistake?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Find the correct estimate of the area of the pond.

[[input:ans2]] \(\text{m}^2\) [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
StepKendiCorrect
1. Number of squares\({@sh1@}\)\({@F@} + \tfrac{1}{2} \times {@P@} = {@est@}\)
2. Area of one square\({@sh2@}\,\text{m}^2\)\({@s@} \times {@s@} = {@s^2@}\,\text{m}^2\)
3. Area\({@sh3@}\,\text{m}^2\)\({@est@} \times {@s^2@} = {@cor@}\,\text{m}^2\)

[[if test="is(er=1)"]]Kendi counted each part square as a whole square. A part square is, on average, about half covered, so it counts as \(\tfrac{1}{2}\).[[elif test="is(er=2)"]]Kendi left out the part squares. Each part square counts as \(\tfrac{1}{2}\), because a part square is, on average, about half covered.[[elif test="is(er=3)"]]Kendi used the length of a side, \({@s@}\,\text{m}\), as the area of a square. A square on the plan stands for a square on the ground, so square the side.[[else]]Kendi used the perimeter of a square, \(4 \times {@s@} = {@4*s@}\,\text{m}\), instead of its area, \({@s@} \times {@s@} = {@s^2@}\,\text{m}^2\).[[/if]]

The area of the pond is about \({@cor@}\,\text{m}^2\).

questiondescription.text:
Area Approximations: finding the mistake in a square count

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.2 (a) / Essential 2.1 (a): Identify the mistake in a worked estimate of an area by counting squares, then give the correct estimate.

Core and Essential

This question is original to this project.

truefeedback.text:
[[if test="is(ch=1)"]]

If Kendi had counted each part square as a whole square, Step 1 would read \({@wv@}\). She wrote \({@sh1@}\), which is right: \({@F@} + \tfrac{1}{2} \times {@P@} = {@est@}\). Look at Step 2.

[[elif test="is(ch=2)"]]

If Kendi had left out the part squares, Step 1 would read \({@wv@}\). She wrote \({@sh1@}\), which is right: \({@F@} + \tfrac{1}{2} \times {@P@} = {@est@}\). Look at Step 2.

[[elif test="is(ch=3)"]]

If Kendi had used the length of a side, Step 2 would read \({@wv@}\,\text{m}^2\). She wrote \({@sh2@}\,\text{m}^2\), which is right: \({@s@} \times {@s@} = {@s^2@}\,\text{m}^2\). Look at Step 1.

[[else]]

If Kendi had used the perimeter of a square, Step 2 would read \({@wv@}\,\text{m}^2\). She wrote \({@sh2@}\,\text{m}^2\), which is right: \({@s@} \times {@s@} = {@s^2@}\,\text{m}^2\). Look at Step 1.

[[/if]]
Kendi's working has a mistake. Work out \({@F@} + \tfrac{1}{2} \times {@P@}\) for Step 1 and the area of a square of side \({@s@}\,\text{m}\) for Step 2, and compare each with what she wrote.

If Kendi had counted each part square as a whole square, Step 1 would read \({@wv@}\). She wrote \({@sh1@}\), so that is not her mistake. Work out what this step should say and compare.

[[elif test="is(ch=2)"]]

If Kendi had left out the part squares, Step 1 would read \({@wv@}\). She wrote \({@sh1@}\), so that is not her mistake. Work out what this step should say and compare.

[[elif test="is(ch=3)"]]

If Kendi had used the length of a side, Step 2 would read \({@wv@}\,\text{m}^2\). She wrote \({@sh2@}\,\text{m}^2\), so that is not her mistake. Work out what this step should say and compare.

[[else]]

If Kendi had used the perimeter of a square, Step 2 would read \({@wv@}\,\text{m}^2\). She wrote \({@sh2@}\,\text{m}^2\), so that is not her mistake. Work out what this step should say and compare.

[[/if]]

truefeedback.text: That is Kendi's answer, which contains the mistake.

falsefeedback.text: Correct the step that has the mistake, then redo Step 3 with the corrected values: (number of squares) \(\times\) (area of one square).
